finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the `f` query parameter is joined to the root with filepath.Join and no containment check. Join cleans `..` segments, so `../../etc/passwd` resolves to /etc/passwd. An unauthenticated remote attacker can read any file the process can read.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: name taken directly from the query string
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd, which escapes the root
file contents returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware, no prefix or containment check, no Base() or Rel() check, no symlink resolution. The handler is registered directly on the default mux at files.go:32. The avatar handler uses filepath.Base, but this one does not.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the query param `f` straight into filepath.Join(root, name) with no containment check, so `../../etc/passwd` cleans to /etc/passwd, and files.go:18 writes the contents to the response on a default-mux handler (files.go:32) with no auth.
